_comment: Turkish terms chosen for the lesson process-models. status: sourced = attested in a Turkish source I opened; chosen = my own choice or rendering; check = weakly attested, needs a Turkish-language reviewer. The only Turkish source opened for this batch is the Turkish Wikipedia article 'İletişim modelleri' (sections on Newcomb, Schramm, Berlo and the classification doğrusal iletim / etkileşim / işlem models); the course books were not opened for these models, so no term below is claimed to come from a course book. Existing terms (feedback, gatekeeping, noise, source, channel, receiver, message, linear-transmission-model) are reused from core.json, what-is-communication.json and lasswell-shannon-weaver.json.

process-model.note: Turkish Wikipedia distinguishes 'doğrusal iletim, etkileşim ve işlem modelleri'. In this lesson 'süreç modeli' is used for the whole group (Schramm, Newcomb, Westley–MacLean, Berlo) because the course title uses it; 'etkileşim' and 'işlem' are the terms of the three-way classification. Needs a Turkish reviewer.

circular-model.note: 'Dairesel' and 'döngüsel' are both natural renderings of 'circular'; neither Schramm text uses 'circular' (see the research notes). 'Schramm modeli' is the plain name used by Turkish Wikipedia.

field-of-experience.note: Turkish Wikipedia: 'deneyim alanı' / 'deneyim alanları'. 'Başvuru çerçevesi' renders Schramm's own 1971 wording 'frame of reference'; 'deneyim daireleri' describes the drawing.

encoder.note: Turkish Wikipedia uses 'kodlama' for the process; 'kodlayıcı' for the role is my choice (core.json has 'kodlama / kodaçımlama' for encoding/decoding, status check).

decoder.note: Turkish Wikipedia: 'kod çözme' for the process; 'kod çözücü' for the role is my choice.

interpreter.note: The third role in the scheme Schramm attributes to Osgood (encoder, decoder, interpreter). Turkish Wikipedia says the receiver 'kodunu çözmeli ve yorumlamalıdır'.

object-of-orientation.note: Westley and MacLean: 'objects of orientation'. Turkish Wikipedia calls Newcomb's X 'konu/nesne' and speaks of 'yönelimler'.

strain-toward-symmetry.note: Wording 'strain toward symmetry' from the NAS memoir of Newcomb and Schramm 1971 ('Newcomb's strain for symmetry'). Turkish Wikipedia describes the same idea as 'gerginlik' and 'denge'. Needs a Turkish reviewer.

advocacy-roles.note: Westley and MacLean's 'As (Advocacy roles)': the communicator who selects and transmits messages purposively. 'Savunucu' is my rendering of 'advocacy'.

behavioral-system.note: Westley and MacLean's 'Bs (Behavioral system roles)': what is usually meant by the receiver or the public; a person, group or social system.

channel-roles.note: Westley and MacLean's 'Cs (Channel roles)': agents of B who select and transmit non-purposively; the gatekeeper role (gatekeeping is in core.json: 'kapı bekçiliği').

purposive-feedback.note: Westley and MacLean's 'purposive' and 'non-purposive' feedback. 'Amaçlı/amaçsız' keeps their word 'purpose'; 'bilinçli/bilinçsiz' would misstate what they mean.

smcr.note: Turkish Wikipedia: 'SMCR modeli' or 'Kaynak-Mesaj-Kanal-Alıcı'. 'İleti' is the glossary form of 'message' in what-is-communication.json.

communication-skills.note: Turkish Wikipedia's rendering of Berlo's first source factor (writing, speaking, reading, listening, thought in Berlo's own list).

attitudes.note: Turkish Wikipedia; Berlo distinguishes attitude toward self, toward the subject matter and toward the receiver.

knowledge-level.note: Turkish Wikipedia uses 'bilgi'; Berlo's own heading is 'Knowledge Level'.

social-cultural-system.note: Turkish Wikipedia: 'sosyal-kültürel sistem'; 'toplumsal-kültürel' is the form used in this lesson.

treatment.note: Berlo's third message factor is 'treatment': the choices the source makes in delivering code and content. Turkish Wikipedia renders it 'davranış', which does not match Berlo's word and is flagged in the lesson; 'işleyiş' is my choice. Needs a Turkish reviewer.

process.note: Berlo's concept of process: no beginning, end or fixed sequence; ingredients affect each other.

transactional-model.note: Turkish Wikipedia: 'doğrusal iletim, etkileşim ve işlem'. Mentioned only in the exam card; no concept page was created for the transactional model.
